category.name: Docs and wiki
category.description: Team documentation, internal wikis and shared knowledge workspaces.
category.audience: Employees and teams documenting decisions, procedures, project plans and institutional knowledge.
category.audienceRationale: Documentation spans business functions; adoption does not require a specialist department. Qualitative potential reach, not a headcount estimate.

pricing.note: Paid Plus exists; page auto-selected EUR 9.50/member/month and billing state was ambiguous. USD entry intentionally unverified; free SaaS tier is not OSS.
Standard public calculator displayed $5.78/user/month on monthly billing; price changes with seat count and billing. Free plan up to 10 users exists.

oss.name: BookStack
oss.classificationReason: Project FAQ explicitly confirms one free open edition, no enterprise/custom edition and no feature locks. Official support is paid; no official managed hosting. Codeberg is now canonical; GitHub remains an active mirror.

health.rsx: Quick analysis completed; overall 6/10. Automated signals only; version-specific security findings not independently adjudicated.

oss.name: Docmost Community
locked: Business license gates SSO, AI, granular page permissions and Confluence importer.
Enterprise adds SCIM, audit logs, SIEM and page verification/review.
oss.classificationReason: AGPL applies to community core; apps/server/src/ee, apps/client/src/ee and packages/ee use commercial license per pinned README. Everyday migration and collaboration controls require Business. README links a cloud version, but current pricing emphasizes self-managed and hosted price is unverified.

health.rsx: Quick analysis completed; overall 5.5/10. Automated signals only; version-specific security findings not independently adjudicated.

oss.name: AppFlowy client core
locked: Current commercial self-hosted server free tier is limited to one user seat per instance and three guest editors.
Commercial server enterprise authentication needs Seed or higher; server is separately licensed.
oss.classificationReason: AGPL client core is OSI, but current production collaboration uses separately commercial server images. Full collaborative self-hosted OSS eligibility is unresolved; archived AGPL AppFlowy-Cloud excluded. Local client remains usable under AGPL. Excluded from default OSS collaboration recommendations pending a clearly eligible maintained full stack.

health.rsx: Quick analysis completed; overall 6.6/10. Automated signals only; version-specific security findings not independently adjudicated.

oss.name: AFFiNE (mixed-license stack; review required)
locked: Official enterprise page says self-hosted Team required for more than 10 seats; multiple admin roles and priority support in Team.
Non-CE backend/native code has commercial EE production and redistribution restrictions.
oss.classificationReason: MIT covers code outside backend/native. Backend EE license explicitly exempts CE-distributed and specified client-side portions under MPL-2.0. Official marketing calls backend source-available, while blogs acknowledge MPL CE carveout. Full current CE boundary not independently reconstructed: do not present full stack as verified OSI OSS. MIT local editor is clearly OSS.

health.rsx: Quick analysis completed; overall 6.7/10. Automated signals only; version-specific security findings not independently adjudicated.

oss.name: Outline (source-available)
locked: Community on-premises edition has limited features; Business and Enterprise sold separately.
Exact matrix checkmark mapping did not survive text extraction; paid migration/AI/security feature allocation requires visual verification.
oss.classificationReason: Pinned license explicitly says it is not an open source license. Additional Use Grant forbids commercial third-party Document Services. Pinned version changes to Apache-2.0 on 2030-10-12; that future conversion does not make current version OSS.

health.rsx: Quick analysis completed; overall 5.1/10. Automated signals only; version-specific security findings not independently adjudicated.

alternatives.migrationNotes: Documentation/wiki use case covered with book/chapter/page hierarchy, roles, API and export options; validate Confluence macros/integrations and rebuild unsupported content.
Useful for the wiki/documentation portion of Notion; hierarchical documentation model rather than Notion database workspace. No verified native Notion importer.
Notion ZIP import preserves page structure; pilot databases, permissions and linked content. Export pages/spaces as Markdown or HTML.
Confluence HTML space ZIP importer is Business-gated; docs claim formatting, hierarchy, internal links, images/attachments and Draw.io diagrams preserved. Test macros and integrations separately.
AGPL client supports documents/databases and local data control. Full team replacement needs separately commercial self-hosted services; do not treat AGPL client as unlimited OSS server.
Docs and canvas approach; local MIT editor is useful, but full self-hosted collaboration has mixed licensing and seat/plan questions. Pilot database parity and export/import round trips.
Docs/whiteboards for shared knowledge; verify EE/CE license scope and procurement before production. Migration compatibility not independently tested.
Knowledge-base replacement candidate under BSL rather than OSS; Confluence importer listed among on-premise features but exact paid-tier placement not verified. API export capabilities documented.
Fits shared documentation; Notion database/workflow parity not claimed. Review BSL Document Service restriction and community edition limits.
